authorization: 2026-10-19 user asks to explore better trajectory encoders and stop tricky auxiliary research
question: Which simple encoder can reliably preserve observed point trajectories under the same decoder and training recipe?
scope: Representation/reconstruction only. Not future forecasting, collision generalization, MAE, policy control, or paper reproduction.

data.source: immutable original206training episodes only; sort by(seed,episode_id), reserve ranks4,9,14,...for codec validation (41episodes/451windows), remaining165episodes/1815windows for codec training
data.future: 20samples from0.1to2.0seconds; true future is deliberately input for reconstruction, never a forecast claim
data.coordinates: point trajectory minus its query current point, metres, conventional past-minus-current and future-minus-current
data.single_sample: one point trajectory, up to20steps; zero-padded coordinates/time plus explicit valid length
data.features_per_step: XYZ divided by one train-only global RMS scale, physical time in seconds, validity bit
data.movement_group: encoded trajectory endpoint displacement magnitude>1cm for either endpoint of the same pin; training/metrics grouping only, not encoder input
data.training_fit_display: all88windows from the first8 codec-training episodes sorted by original seed; no held-out episode included
data.legacy_validation: initial data-preparation draft read original16validation windows, then discarded before formal training because historical scene trajectories were entirely quiet; formal comparison does not use that draft
data.validation_split: episode-disjoint deterministic1in5holdout of originaltraining trajectories; no split chosen by reconstruction scores

architecture.time_pool: original FiLM time-pooling encoder modules, freshly initialized; new common decoder and input normalization, not the historical full tokenizer recipe
architecture.gru: unidirectional one-layer GRU5->192; last valid hidden192->256
architecture.tcn: 5->80 projection; four causal residual Conv1d blocks, kernel3/dilations1,2,4,8, GELU; last valid hidden80->256
architecture.common_decoder: 256->256->60, GELU between linear layers; reshaped20x3; valid steps scored
architecture.common_initialization: decoder parameters copied exactly within each seed; encoder shapes and counts differ and are disclosed
architecture.raw_reference: flatten20x5observed features and zero-pad100to256; inverse returns coordinates exactly up to normalization arithmetic; no learned weights
architecture.no_information_bottleneck_claim: 256dimensions exceed both10x3and20x3coordinates; this tests preservation and optimization, not compression

training.balanced_group_sampling: 32trajectories per group per step; identical saved index plan for all arms within seed
training.schedule: 200step linear warmup then cosine decay to0.0001
training.loss: normalized XYZ MSE, valid times only, trajectory mean then equal group mean via balanced sampling
training.selection: fixed last5000step only; no validation selection, no hyperparameter sweep, no automatic extension
training.precision: FP32, noTF32; encoder comparisons are nominal interface matches, not equal parameter or wall-time matches

evaluation.primary: mean of eight per-group ADEs, each first averaged within episode; also every group and per-seed result
evaluation.decision: Call a candidate accurately preserving trajectories only if all3seeds have all supported validation groups ADE<=1mm and FDE<=3mm. This is an engineering target, not a paper rule. Report failures unchanged.
evaluation.interpretation: Prefer the simplest successful representation. Reconstruction does not establish best downstream dynamics. No significance or unseen-environment claims from reused16validation episodes.

compute: one rechecked development GPU, sequential runs, allocator<=6GiB; never change others processes
closed_branch: previous history-completion optimization remains closed; this is a separately authorized encoder study
planned_followup: none automatic; no long-horizon dynamics or auxiliary-loss run in this protocol
protocol_revision_note: Amended before formal training: deterministic episode holdout includes moving histories unlike original16validation anchors. Early4-step module checks are disposable; no candidate comparison results informed this split.
